narrative.overview:
The site is one more window of Bardo, not a separate marketing brand. It sits on the near-neutral graphite the Mac draws in dark mode (the same ground as the owner's portfolio covers, #121016), sets Geist tight and bold, and lets the real app speak: whole components cut from real captures float on that ground with a soft, deep shadow, readable at their own size. Everything else stays quiet so the screenshots carry the page.

Colour is a signal, never decoration. The bard's purple appears as brand and focus (focus rings, text selection, caret, and the 3D icon itself). Blue, orange and green appear only where speakers do: in the captures and in the speaker legend. The whole site is dark; there is no light band.

Density is calm and editorial without the editorial skeleton: one idea per section, a headline of a few words, one lead sentence, then the picture. Sections alternate text and picture on an asymmetric 4:7 grid; lists of facts are ruled ledgers, not cards.
keyCharacteristics: Dark graphite ground with three tonal steps; hairline rules instead of boxes.
Geist Variable 700 at tight negative tracking for every heading; 400 for reading.
Real app components, whole and legible, floating with `shadow-float`.
Purple only for brand and focus; speaker hues only for speakers.
Pill-shaped controls; generously rounded floating pictures; 28px bands.
One authored entrance (the hero window); everything else is plain state transitions.

rules.name: The Colour Means Something Rule
rules.body: Purple is brand and focus; blue, orange and green are speakers. If a colour on a new surface cannot say which of those it is, it is graphite.

rules.name: The All Graphite Rule
rules.body: The site is dark from top to bottom: no light band, no appearance switch.

rules.name: The Monochrome Primary Rule
rules.body: The primary action is near-white on graphite (`text` fill, `ground` label), not purple. The brand colour stays rare so focus remains visible.

rules.name: The Short Measure Rule
rules.body: Headings are capped in `ch` (display 11-14ch, headline 14-16ch) and leads at 30-52ch, so every section reads as one idea.

rules.name: The Numbers Align Rule
rules.body: Sizes, versions and step numerals use `tabular-nums`.

rules.name: The Only Things That Float Are the App Rule
rules.body: Shadows belong to app windows and components shown on the page. Sections, panels, ledgers and the footer are flat and use tone or a hairline instead.

dos: **Do** use the 3D bard app icon (`assets/marca/icono-bardo*.webp`, favicons and touch icons derived from it) as the only logo, at 32px in the nav, 56px in the footer and 144px or larger in closing and download heroes.
**Do** show the real app as whole, legible components (UI text at least 11px on screen) floating on graphite with the Float shadow, with a phone-specific source for small screens.
**Do** keep Bard Purple for focus, selection, caret and the icon; keep speaker hues for speakers.
**Do** set facts as ruled ledgers with tabular numbers instead of cards.
**Do** keep one idea per section: a short bold headline, one lead sentence, one picture.
**Do** take every page width from `shell` and every gutter from `--gutter`.
donts: **Don't** use the flat logo kit in `design/logo/kit` (or any flat wordmark or redraw of the bard) anywhere on the site.
**Don't** fill buttons, backgrounds or panels with Bard Purple, or use speaker colours for anything that is not a speaker.
**Don't** introduce a second light surface or a light page theme; light lives only in the appearance band.
**Don't** put shadows on sections, panels, ledgers or the footer; only app pictures float.
**Don't** return to the editorial marketing skeleton the site replaced: no serif hero, no bento grid, no slogan band.
**Don't** crop captures into strips where UI text drops below legibility, or cut through sentences and buttons.
**Don't** add another entrance animation; the hero window's is the only one.
